about.title: Oroville Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Butte County recorded traffic deaths in Oroville within the most recent reporting year, a reminder that even a small city's busy corridors carry real risk. Feather River Boulevard, Olive Highway, and both stretches of Oroville Dam Boulevard see steady traffic, and Tuesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to bring more reported collisions than other times. When a crash on any of these roads takes a family member's life, California law allows certain survivors to pursue a wrongful death claim separate from any criminal proceeding against the at-fault driver. Standing is limited by law, generally starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and extending to other dependents or heirs when no closer survivor exists. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect grieving families in Oroville with an independent attorney who can explain what the law allows and what deadlines apply, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: What Oroville Families Should Know About Wrongful Death Law

items.title: Strict Filing Deadlines Apply
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity involving a public road may require action much sooner. Missing these windows can end a family's right to recover, so timing matters from the start.

items.title: Only Certain Survivors Can File
items.desc: State law limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, usually starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and moving to other dependents or heirs if none exist. An attorney can help clarify where your family stands before any claim moves forward.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond Funeral Costs
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. These are real, recognized losses under California law, not just symbolic ones.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation to explain who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Oroville?
items.answer: The general deadline is two years from the date of death, but claims involving a government-maintained road, such as some sections of Oroville Dam Boulevard, may carry a much shorter notice window. It's worth speaking with an attorney soon after a loss to avoid missing key dates.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim replace a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges the driver may face. The civil case focuses on compensating the family, while the criminal case addresses potential punishment for the driver. Both can proceed independently of each other.
